description: The common record emitted by every checker, gate, scan and grade in the Open Door stack. A record states what was measured, by what method and version, against what targets, with what verdict, evidence and limits. It is a measurement record, not a warranty.

body_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical record body (the record serialised without this field), so later edits are visible.

chain.description: Ledger position of this record, when the record is written to a ledger. Records in a partition form a hash chain: each record names the body hash of the previous record in its partition, so removal or alteration of any record breaks the chain for every later record. The first record in a partition uses the genesis hash: SHA-256 of the string 'GENESIS-' followed by the partition_id.

chain_hash.description: body_sha256 of the previous record in this partition, or the partition's genesis hash for its first record.

partition_id.description: The ledger partition this record belongs to (e.g. a task, a session, a subject's history).

seq_num.description: Monotonically increasing position within the partition, assigned by the ledger at write time, starting at 1.

context.description: Links to neighbouring records and contracts, when they exist.

epoch_ref.description: Identifier of the version record for the issuing system's state at write time (e.g. an EPOCH-style release record ID), so the exact versions in force when this record was issued can be reconstructed later. Version records are records like any other and follow this same schema.

evidence.description: Where the underlying evidence can be inspected.

issued_at.description: When the record was issued, ISO 8601.

issued_by.description: Who or what issued the record: an operator, a service, or a named tool run.

limitations.description: What this record does not establish. A record that hides its limits is not a proof.

measurements.description: The measured values, each against its target. Empty only when the record type carries no numeric measures (e.g. a gate decision).

environment.description: Conditions that affect the result, stated exactly (e.g. ambient temperature band for a hardware battery).

procedure.description: Reference to the procedure or battery that was run, specific enough for another operator to repeat it.

record_id.description: Stable, unique identifier for this record. Never reused.

record_type.description: Which kind of proof this record carries.

risk_level.description: The assessed risk level of the subject or operation at issue time, in the issuing standard's own scale (e.g. 'R1', 'high', 'SEV2'). It sits inside the sealed record body, so the risk assessment travels with the verdict it governed and cannot be detached or revised silently. After the S5 seal principle in the CHIN architecture (Sovereign Archive, Rank 2): risk level encoding belongs in the seal, not beside it.

standard.description: The standard this record was issued under.

version.description: Semantic version of the standard, e.g. 1.0.0.

subject.description: The thing measured, bound as exactly as the domain allows: a skill version, a tool version, a task, an output, or a hardware serial number.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the subject's canonical content, when the subject is digital.

serial.description: Serial number or equivalent unique identifier, when the subject is a physical unit.

supersedes.description: The record_id this record corrects or replaces, or null. Corrections are new records, never silent edits.

deficits.description: Every disclosed deficit, line by line. A passing record with deficits lists them here; they are never hidden.

outcome.description: The verdict in the issuing standard's own terms, e.g. pass, fail, a letter grade, allow, deny, escalate.

title: Proof Record
